title: At a fixed plaintext budget, does spreading the training data over more content families improve encoder identification on a family the model has never seen? The family-diversity curve (FDC) at 4096 with 0003's fixed recipes and 0014's searched logistic: for each of the eight content families and each family count k in {1, 2, 4, 7}, fit on 4900 source chunks (every pool row of each) drawn evenly from the k families that follow it in the sealed order, score once on the held-out family's sealed evaluation rows, stitch the eight readings into one mixture per k, and read the slope of the mixture against log2(k) against 0.005 per doubling; a single-family depth arm, a preceding-family arm and the standardised logistic's own curve are banked beside it.

scope.one_line: One corpus (corpus A, data/pivot/full_c4096.npz, the 0003 corpus, not rebuilt), one seed (20260825), one plaintext budget (4900 source chunks per fit, every pool row of each chunk), four family counts (1, 2, 4, 7), eight held-out families, 0003's three fixed recipes plus 0014's searched logistic L3 (standardised inputs, C 1.0, 1000 iterations) as a fourth fixed role, 0003's sealed evaluation set (260000 rows from 10000 held-out chunks) scored once per fit; two informational arms (single-family depth at 2450, 1225 and 700 chunks; the preceding family at k = 1). It asks whether the transfer failure 0015 measured is a matter of how many content types the model has seen: with the plaintext budget held fixed, does accuracy on an unseen family rise with the number of families the budget is spread over?
scope.why_this_is_the_biggest_open_risk: 0015 bounded the headline: 0003's recipe fitted on seven families identifies the encoder on the eighth at 0.0859 against a bar of 0.0885, and a raw logistic does slightly better (0.0928). 0015 stated as not covered 'whether a recipe trained on more families would transfer better'. That is the data-collection question a reader has next: is transfer bought by more content types, or is the signal bound to the families it was fitted on, so that more of the same kind of data would not help? The corpus can answer it at seven families and below without new data. Either answer is published at the same size; a DIVERSITY_FLAT says that more families of this kind will not, at this rate, fix 0015's failure; a DIVERSITY_HELPS says diversity is a lever, bounded to seven families and this corpus.
scope.corpus: data/pivot/full_c4096.npz exactly as 0003 left it: 1300000 rows from 50000 source chunks 0..49999, 1108 features, carve 4096 by sealed cache identity (the cache carries no build metadata): y sha256 2b70426881e569f303c400b8dc2b3cb69f30dbe2e36a93dff56df54df9acf093, g sha256 eda31b7cfa24640dff694c00e62849537490c9572966a5247d1f5127800e4df9. A row's family is FAMILIES[chunk_id % 8] with FAMILIES = ["gutenberg", "base64", "binary", "code", "csv", "json", "log", "mixed"], the corpus builder's rule.
scope.seed: 20260825 throughout, as in 0003, 0014 and 0015: the grouped split, the pool order and the null-label shuffle (drawn from the split's generator after the split, as in 0015) all come from it.
scope.design: The sealed split is 0003's (grouped_split(seed 20260825, eval_frac 0.2, cap 800000)): 260000 evaluation rows from 10000 chunks, an 800000-row pool from 40000 chunks in generator order, with per-family pool counts of {"gutenberg": 4981, "base64": 4986, "binary": 5001, "code": 5025, "csv": 5034, "json": 4990, "log": 4971, "mixed": 5012} chunks and {"gutenberg": 99712, "base64": 99440, "binary": 100103, "code": 100346, "csv": 100560, "json": 99929, "log": 99527, "mixed": 100383} rows. The BUDGET is 4900 source chunks per fit, counted in plaintexts because that is what a corpus costs: every pool row of a chosen chunk is taken (the pool holds about 20 of the 26 encoder variants of each chunk, so a fit sees about 98000 rows, 97797 to 99226 across the fixed-budget folds), and along the curve the number of encoder variants per plaintext is held at the pool's rather than traded against plaintext count (a row-level rule would take about 20 variants of 5000 chunks at k = 1 and about 3 variants of 5000 chunks at k = 7, varying plaintexts and pairing along k; found in the pre-freeze review). For each held-out family f in the sealed order and each family count k in [1, 2, 4, 7], the training subset is the k families that FOLLOW f cyclically in the sealed family order (gutenberg, base64, binary, code, csv, json, log, mixed), nested in k; each chosen family contributes its FIRST 4900/k chunks by first appearance in pool order (4900, 2450, 1225, 700 chunks — exact for all four counts; 4900 is below the smallest per-family pool chunk count, 4971), with every pool row of those chunks, and the union is kept in pool order so the incumbent's last-10% early-stopping validation split is a mix of the chosen families in generator order; each family's chunk sets are nested across k. Four fits per (f, k) in the order majority, logistic, model, logistic_l3 (the standardised logistic last: it scales the block in place and the machinery refills the block from the cache afterwards, probe-checked, as in 0014), each scored once on the whole sealed evaluation set; the per-family accuracies are banked for every fit, and the fit's READING is its held-out family's accuracy. The mixture at k for a role is the accuracy over all 260000 evaluation rows where row i's correctness is taken from the (f, k) fit that held out i's family; it is banked to 4 decimals and re-derived by the reader from the per-example vectors and the banked chunk ids. The CURVE for a role is the mixture at k against log2(k) (0, 1, 2, 2.807355); its ordinary-least-squares slope over the four points, in accuracy per doubling of families, is computed by the reader from the four banked 4-decimal mixtures and rounded to 6 decimals; the bar is read on the model's slope. Two informational arms, fitted with the same four recipes and scored the same way, separate what the curve entangles. DEPTH: for each f, the single successor family alone at 2450, 1225 and 700 chunks (its first chunks in pool order, nested), so that with k = 1's 4900-chunk fit the depth curve holds the family count at one and varies per-family depth over the same sizes the fixed-budget curve spreads over k families; family_effect_at_matched_depth(k) = mixture(k families at 4900/k chunks each) - mixture(one family at 4900/k chunks) is banked per k, and row_effect_within_family = mixture(one family at 4900) - mixture(one family at 700). PREDECESSOR: for each f, k = 1 refitted with the family that PRECEDES f cyclically at 4900 chunks; composition_spread_k1 = mixture(successor rule) - mixture(predecessor rule) is banked as the composition-sensitivity reading. Neither arm enters the bar. One reproduction control precedes the folds: M1 fitted on the FIRST 100000 pool rows — 0003's 100000-row rung, the same rows in the same order, with the same last-10% validation convention — must score within 0.005 of 0003's banked 0.1965 (artifacts/pivot/deflate_curve.json): the clause checks pool order, machinery, environment and evaluation set against a banked rung, and does not place the folds on the ladder (the rung is 100000 rows scattered over about 37000 chunks; a fold is about 98000 rows over 4900 chunks); the sealed row hashes and the recipe hash (val 'frag') certify row identity and convention, and the anchor certifies machinery, environment and evaluation set. A null control follows: M1 fitted on the first 20000 pool rows (0003's and 0014's null block) with labels shuffled by the split's generator must score at or below chance + 0.02 on the sealed set; 0014's 0.0383 on the same block and shuffle and 0003's 0.0389 are banked as informational drift references. The curve's abscissa is log2(k) at 6 decimals, [0, 1, 2, 2.807355], the same literal in the runner and the reader, so the two run the identical slope arithmetic on identical floats; the reader's own slope is the verdict's and the runner's banked slope must agree with it within 1e-6. The number of boosting iterations each incumbent fit ran (fit_info.n_iter) is banked per fold and listed per k as n_iter_by_k, informational, so the curve can be read against training length.
scope.subset_rule_stated_and_its_confound: Family COUNT and family COMPOSITION cannot be separated with eight families at this cost: every k = 1 point is one particular pairing, and the curve's shape depends on which families follow which. The rule is fixed by the corpus builder's family order, which predates every preregistration in this chain, and is applied identically to every held-out family, so at every k each family appears as a source in exactly k of the eight training sets (the source marginal is balanced at the mixture level); that is why the bar is read on the mixture and not on any family's own curve. The predecessor arm bounds the composition sensitivity at k = 1 with one alternative pairing per family; a rule that averaged over compositions (every subset of size k) would cost 7 + 21 + 35 + 1 fits per held-out family per role and is not run. The per-family curves are banked so a reader can see which pairings carry the mixture. The fixed budget entangles family count with per-family depth (4900 chunks of one family against 700 chunks of each of seven); the depth arm measures the per-family depth effect at the same sizes so the two can be read apart, and a DIVERSITY_FLAT is stated as 'at a fixed plaintext budget, spreading it over more families does not pay', not as 'families do not matter'.

scope.recipes_are_0003s: M1, L1 and U1 verbatim from 0015's sealed recipes (0014's roster; params hashes in the reader): the incumbent HGB (learning rate 0.15, 63 leaves, 200 iterations with patience 10 on the last 10% of rows), LogisticRegression(max_iter=400) on raw features, DummyClassifier(most_frequent); and L3 verbatim from 0014's sealed roster (LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=1000) on standardised inputs, 0014's selected logistic at 0.2317 in-distribution), added because 0015 found the raw logistic transferring better than the incumbent while hitting its 400-iteration cap in every fold, so a converged, standardised linear rule is the more informative comparator under transfer (pre-freeze review). Nothing is searched or selected; the bar is on M1, the standardised logistic's curve is a named reading. The four recipe objects are byte-identical to their sealed sources, including their 'why' strings (which describe their roles in 0014 and 0015: the raw logistic's mentions 0003's frozen-set bar and a reproduction clause 0016 does not have), so that every params hash is the same literal as in the earlier readers; 0016's only reproduction clause is the incumbent on the 100000-row rung.
scope.what_the_curve_measures_and_does_not: It measures, at 4900 source chunks and 4096 bytes, how the accuracy of 0003's recipe on an unseen family changes with the number of families the budget is spread over, from one to seven, with the depth and predecessor arms beside it. It does not measure the row axis under transfer beyond the depth arm and one derived comparison (0015's k = 7 point at about 700000 rows, about 5000 chunks per family, is banked beside the k = 7 point here at 700 chunks per family); it does not measure transfer to content outside the corpus builder's eight families, to more than seven training families, to other carve sizes or other encoder sets; a DIVERSITY_HELPS says 'among these families, diversity at a fixed plaintext budget moves transfer at this rate for 0003's M1 recipe', not that the signal is universal. The incompressible families (base64, binary, mixed) sit near the byte-identity collision ceiling in-distribution and are expected near chance at every k; the mixture counts them.

reference_0015_lofo_at_full_rows.use: informational: the row axis under transfer, derived by the reader as the model's k = 7 mixture at 700 chunks per family minus 0.0859 (about 5000 chunks per family)

scope.cost: EXTRAPOLATION from banked fits. The pre-freeze anchor check fitted M1 on 100000 rows in 341.4 s over 49 boosting iterations at 3 threads, nice 10 (about 7 s per iteration); 0015 banked 804 to 846 s for L1 at about 700000 rows (929.7 s for 400 iterations at 800000), so about 120 s at 98000 rows. 0014 banked 1164.3 s for L3 at 800000 rows (728 iterations), so about 150 s at 98000 rows. Fixed-budget folds: 32 x (about 340 s M1 + about 120 s L1 + about 150 s L3 + 0 s majority) about 19500 s; depth arm: 24 folds at 14000 to 49500 rows, about 24 x 220 s = 5300 s; predecessor arm: 8 folds at about 98000 rows, about 4900 s; reproduction about 340 s; null about 60 s; 66 gathers of 14000 to 100000 rows from the memmapped cache plus one probe-checked refill per fold after the standardised fit, seconds each. Typical total about 30000 s (8.5 h) of fit time; the raw logistic reaching its 400-iteration cap is the typical case (every 0015 fold did), not a worst case. Worst case: every HGB fit to its 200-iteration cap (200/49 of the measured anchor, about 1400 s at 98000 rows) and every standardised logistic to its 1000-iteration cap: about 40 x 1400 + 24 x 700 + 40 x 200 + 24 x 100 + 40 x 210 + 24 x 100 = 94000 s (26 h); no fit has a time cap. Memory (anonymous RSS): a 98000 x 1108 float64 block is 0.87 GB, the evaluation block 1.15 GB, HGB's binned copy and bin-mapper subsample under 0.3 GB: the anchor check peaked at 2.8 GB; launch precondition 6.0 GB MemAvailable (0014 and 0015 asked 12.0 GB for their 7.09 GB pool blocks; nothing here gathers more than 100000 rows); kill threshold 13.0 GB anonymous as before. The runner refuses to launch when sklearn, numpy or python differ from the sealed versions, because the reader voids every record on a version mismatch and a refusal costs nothing where a VOID after hours would. Every fit scores the sealed set, so NOT RUN is reachable only by a failed launch precondition or three launches without a new checkpoint before the first one exists. Outputs: the artifact about 1 MB; the scores file about 77 MB (about 290 per-example vectors of 260000 characters), committed once at the final bank; 258 checkpoints of a few hundred KB each committed as they land.
scope.sealed_set_disclosure: This is the fourth preregistration scored on 0003's sealed evaluation set: 0003 scored it 12 times, 0006 for top-k, 0014 10 times plus 10 in a smoke confirm, 0015 27 times plus its smokes; 0016 adds 258 scorings (128 fixed-budget fits, 96 depth-arm fits, 32 predecessor fits, 1 reproduction, 1 null), all of them fixed recipes with no selection, and its smoke runs add their own, counted in artifacts/pivot/engineering_log_0016.json. The reproduction anchor was checked once before the freeze on this machinery (M1 on the first 100000 pool rows, scored on the sealed set, in the scratchpad): top-1 0.1965, exactly 0003's banked rung, in 341.4 s over 49 boosting iterations at 2.36 GB anonymous RSS (the record is kept in the session scratchpad and the value is restated in artifacts/pivot/engineering_log_0016.json; that check built its candidate from the incumbent's parameters without 0015's recipe object around them, so its params hash is not the sealed M1 hash, but its parameters and validation convention equal the sealed recipe's key for key); disclosed here so that the control clause is known to be reachable by an honest run, the failure class 0015's pre-freeze review caught on its logistic anchor.
scope.expected_outcome_stated_in_advance: Genuinely uncertain, and stated so, with the prior leaning to DIVERSITY_FLAT. Prior: the structured families gain from structured neighbours (code held out sees csv first; csv sees json first), gutenberg, base64 and binary sit near chance at every k, and mixed is a mixture of the others. The whole dynamic range under transfer is small: 0015's seven-family mixture at about 5000 chunks per family is 0.0859, so the k = 7 point here (700 chunks per family) is expected below that, perhaps 0.06 to 0.08, and the k = 1 point (one family at 4900 chunks) near 0.045 to 0.06; the end-to-end difference is plausibly 0.005 to 0.03, i.e. a slope of 0.002 to 0.011 per doubling, and the bar of 0.005 sits inside that range (about a third of the plausible headroom and about 25 evaluation-noise standard errors of a mixture over 260000 rows). In-distribution a doubling of rows buys 0.0148 (0003's slope x log10(2)); the bar is calibrated to the transfer regime, not to that. A DIVERSITY_FLAT does not revise 0015, 0014 or 0003; it says that at a fixed plaintext budget, spreading it over more content types of this kind is not, at this rate, what fixes transfer for 0003's recipe. The depth arm is expected to show per-family depth mattering (a single family at 4900 chunks above the same family at 700); how much of the fixed-budget slope survives after that is the reading the arm exists for. The standardised logistic's curve is expected above the raw logistic's at every k (0014 banked 0.2317 against 0.1352 in-distribution) and is banked as a reading, not a clause; whether its slope exceeds the incumbent's is open.
scope.what_a_fail_would_mean_for_the_record: A DIVERSITY_FLAT is filed as a second boundary of the headline in VERDICT.md, README.md and every outbound document at full size: the encoder signature 0003's recipe learns is bound to the families it is fitted on, and spreading a fixed plaintext budget over more of the corpus builder's families does not move accuracy on an unseen one by 0.005 per doubling. No correction is owed, because no document claims that diversity would fix transfer; 0015's 'not covered' becomes 'measured, and it does not, at this budget and rate'.
scope.what_this_does_not_cover: Other carve sizes, searched model recipes, content outside the eight families, more than seven training families, the row axis under transfer beyond the depth arm and one derived comparison, compositions other than the successor and predecessor rules, the standardised logistic on 0015's full folds (a separate preregistration), calibration, or a buyer. Nothing here establishes a buyer, a customer, a user or a partner.

model.why: 0003's incumbent verbatim (run_study.py make_model 'hgb', run_carve.py's explicit last-10% validation split); every other parameter at the sklearn 1.9.0 default

logistic.why: 0003's logistic verbatim (LogisticRegression(max_iter=400), lbfgs, C 1.0, raw features): the frozen-set bar at 0.1392; its confirmatory reproduction within 0.005 is a validity clause

majority.why: no hyperparameter; confirmatory fit only, as in 0003 (0.0385 banked)

logistic_l3.why: standardised inputs with C 1.0: the single most standard fix for an lbfgs logistic on 1108 unscaled hand-engineered columns

null.rows_are: the first 20000 pool rows, labels shuffled by the split's generator

reference_null_drift.use: informational drift references beside the null reading; the clause is chance + 0.02

scope.families_are_generators: Seven of the eight content families are parametric generators in tools/pivot/corpus.py sharing one vocabulary (base64, binary, code, csv, json, log, mixed); one (gutenberg) is real prose. The curve is therefore a statement about diversity among this builder's generators, read over family counts one to seven under one sealed ordering, and is not extrapolated past seven families or to real content types; that bound is written into both verdict texts.

reference_0014_l3.use: informational: L3's in-distribution value beside its transfer curve

scope_parameters_sealed.passes_if: preregistration == '0016-fdc-4096'; smoke is False; stage == 'run'; the corpus block equals the sealed constants (carve 4096 by sealed cache identity, chunk size 32768, offset 0, chunk ids 0..49999, 50000 chunks, 1300000 rows, 1108 features, the y and g hashes); the banked protocol equals the sealed protocol key by key and hashes to the reader's PROTOCOL_SHA256; the banked recipes hash to the reader's RECIPES_SHA256; n_classes 26 and chance 0.038462.

sealed_sets.passes_if: The banked partition equals the sealed constants field by field: eval (260000 rows, 10000 chunks, idx and y hashes), pool (800000 rows, idx, y and sorted hashes, per-family row and chunk counts), the reproduction rung (100000 rows, idx and sorted hashes), the null block's sorted hash, the budget 4900 chunks, the family counts [1, 2, 4, 7], the depth sizes [4900, 2450, 1225, 700], the subset rule, and for every fold — the 32 fixed-budget (family, k) folds, the 24 depth folds and the 8 predecessor folds — the chosen families, chunks per family, training row count, training index and sorted hashes, chunk count and the per-family row and chunk maps.

no_leakage.passes_if: For every fold the banked counts train_rows_of_heldout_family, train_rows_outside_chosen_families, train_chunks_shared_with_eval and train_rows_in_eval are 0; the reader recomputes the chosen families from the sealed family order (the k successors of the held-out family; the first successor alone for the depth arm; the predecessor for the predecessor arm) and requires the banked per-family chunk map to be exactly 4900/k (or the depth size) for each chosen family and 0 for every other family, and the per-family row map to be 0 outside the chosen families; every fit record's fit_rows_sha256 and fit_rows_sorted_sha256 equal the fold's sealed hashes with n_fit_rows equal to the sealed count and the preregistered seed; the reproduction record carries the sealed 100000-row hashes and the null record the sealed sorted hash.

complete_one_scoring_per_fit.passes_if: complete is True; all 256 fold records (128 fixed-budget, 96 depth, 32 predecessor; four roles each), the reproduction record and the null record have status 'fit' with finite top-1, non-gutenberg top-1 and eight finite per-family accuracies; every name has exactly one 'completed' event in the ledger; every fold record and the reproduction record has a per-example vector in the scores file that is a string of exactly 260000 '0'/'1' characters; each fold record's stage is 'fdc:<family>:k<k>', 'depth:<family>:c<chunks>' or 'pred:<family>:k1' as its name says; each record's params hash equals the sealed hash of its recipe; the banked environment (threads 3, nice 10, sklearn 1.9.0, numpy 2.4.6) matches in every record.

reproduces_0003_100k_rung.passes_if: abs(incumbent_100k_refit_top1 - 0.1965) <= 0.005, compared as round(abs(a - b), 6) <= 0.005 on an accuracy banked to 4 decimals (0.2015 passes, 0.2016 fails), for M1 fitted on the first 100000 pool rows with its last 10% as the early-stopping validation split, scored once on the sealed set. 0.1965 is 0003's banked 100000-row rung (artifacts/pivot/deflate_curve.json rungs[2]); 0014 reproduced the 800000-row rung exactly under this machinery, and the anchor was checked once before the freeze (scope.sealed_set_disclosure). Failure is VOID: the run is not measuring 0003's pipeline at this row scale.

null_control.passes_if: shuffled_label_accuracy <= chance_accuracy + 0.02, the control being M1 fitted on the sealed 20000-row null block with shuffled labels and scored on the sealed set.

mixture_and_curve_arithmetic.passes_if: The reader recomputes every stitched mixture — each role at each k, each depth size and the predecessor k = 1 — from the eight per-example vectors and the banked evaluation chunk ids (family = FAMILIES[chunk % 8]) and requires the banked mixture_top1, mixture_top1_non_gutenberg, structured_four_top1 and per_family values to equal the recomputation at 4 decimals and each banked stitched vector to equal the stitched one; requires each role's mixture_top1_by_k to be the four fixed-budget mixtures in the sealed order of family counts, its slope_per_doubling to equal the ordinary-least-squares slope of the four 4-decimal mixtures against the sealed abscissa log2(k) = [0, 1, 2, 2.807355] (6-decimal literals shared by runner and reader), rounded to 6 decimals (the reader's own computation is the verdict's; the banked value must agree within 1e-6), its end_difference, depth readings (mixture_top1_by_chunks, row_effect_within_family, row_effect_per_doubling_of_chunks), family_effect_at_matched_depth per k and composition_spread_k1 to equal the reader's recomputation at 6 decimals; the banked fdc_slope_per_doubling, fdc_mixture_top1_by_k and fdc_end_difference must be the model role's, and fdc_slope_model_minus_logistic the difference of the two slopes.

diversity.passes_if: the reader's recomputed slope of the model's fixed-budget mixture against log2(families), rounded to 6 decimals, is >= 0.005 - 1e-9, i.e. 0003's M1 recipe gains at least 0.005 in accuracy on an unseen family per doubling of the number of training families at a fixed plaintext budget of 4900 chunks (0.005 passes, 0.004999 fails). Verdict DIVERSITY_HELPS if it passes, DIVERSITY_FLAT if not; the verdict is a statement about 0003's M1 recipe at this budget, over family counts one to seven under the sealed successor rule, with no extrapolation past seven. The end difference, the raw logistic's, standardised logistic's and majority's curves, the depth arm, the predecessor arm, the per-family and structured-four readings, the comparison with 0015's full-row mixture and the cluster intervals are banked as readings and gate nothing.

arms: REPRODUCTION: M1 on the first 100000 pool rows (0003's 100000-row rung), scored once on the sealed set; must give 0.1965 within 0.005.
NULL: M1 on the sealed 20000-row null block (0014's) with shuffled labels, scored once; at or below chance + 0.02.

THIRTY-TWO FIXED-BUDGET FOLDS, in the sealed family order gutenberg, base64, binary, code, csv, json, log, mixed and within each family k = 1, 2, 4, 7: majority, then logistic, then model, then the standardised logistic, each fitted on 4900 source chunks (every pool row of each) drawn evenly from the k families that follow the held-out family and scored once on the sealed set. The reading is the held-out family's accuracy; the eight readings at each k stitch into the mixture at k, and the four mixtures make the curve the verdict is read from.

TWENTY-FOUR DEPTH FOLDS (informational): for each held-out family, its first successor alone at 2450, 1225 and 700 chunks, the same four recipes, scored once each; with the k = 1 fold they give the single-family depth curve over the sizes the fixed-budget curve spreads over k families.

EIGHT PREDECESSOR FOLDS (informational): for each held-out family, k = 1 refitted with the family that precedes it at 4900 chunks, the same four recipes, scored once each; the successor-minus-predecessor spread at k = 1 is the composition-sensitivity reading.
stop_rules: DIVERSITY_FLAT is published at the same size as DIVERSITY_HELPS would have been, as a boundary of the headline in every document that states the headline.

A validity or control failure is VOID: the clause is named, nothing is counted in either direction; a VOID run may be resumed from its checkpoints under the identical invocation and is never re-parameterised.

NOT RUN is reachable only before the first checkpoint and only by the three-launches-without-a-new-checkpoint rule; it is filed as artifacts/pivot/fdc_4096_not_run.json, the reader prints it and exits 2, and it is not a verdict. A failed launch precondition (threads, nice, disk, MemAvailable) refuses to launch and counts as a launch without a checkpoint. A lost checkpoint directory after the first checkpoint is a published VOID, not a fresh start.

Once any checkpoint exists the artifact exists at the sealed path with complete false and reads VOID naming the missing fits until every fit is banked; abandonment after that point is a published VOID.

No recipe, family count, budget, subset, arm, fold or role is added, removed or re-parameterised after freeze: the recipes hash to a literal in the frozen reader and sit under the sealed scope; a record whose params hash is off-recipe or whose rows are off-seal reads VOID.

The sealed evaluation set is scored exactly once per fit; no fold is re-fitted; interruptions are counted, never turned into a status; infeasible_memory is stamped only on a caught MemoryError or a kill at the 13.0 GB anonymous-RSS threshold and reads VOID.

The 0.005 bar is not lowered, the abscissa is not changed, the mixture is not re-weighted, no family and no k is dropped from the curve, the depth and predecessor arms and the logistic curves never enter the bar, and absence, NaN or inf read as VOID.
This cannot revise 0003, 0006, 0007, 0011, 0014 or 0015; revises_0003_0014_0015 and establishes_a_buyer are emitted False unconditionally; no customer, user, partner or buyer is claimed.

Cost is banked beside the result (fit seconds, ru_maxrss and heartbeat anonymous RSS per record, launches, interruptions, refills, the environment) and gates nothing in the reader; every cost figure in scope.cost is an extrapolation and is replaced by the banked figures in the record.

The corpus, the evaluation set, the pool, the reproduction rung, the null block and every fold are one draw and are not redrawn; smoke runs write only to the scratchpad, are stamped smoke true, and read VOID.

thesis.what_would_make_it_fail_honestly: A fixed-budget mixture that does not rise with the number of families: near-chance readings on gutenberg, base64 and binary at every k, structured families gaining little from structured neighbours, and a slope under 0.005 per doubling — the signature of eight family-bound encoder signatures that a fixed plaintext budget cannot spread; the depth arm then says how much of the flatness is per-family depth displaced by diversity.
thesis.what_a_pass_would_mean: That at a fixed plaintext budget diversity among this builder's families moves transfer at 0.005 or more per doubling of families for 0003's M1 recipe, over family counts one to seven under the sealed successor rule: content variety is a lever on the failure 0015 measured within those bounds; nothing about universality, nothing past seven families, and nothing about the searched recipes or the logistics, whose curves are banked beside it.
thesis.what_neither_outcome_means: Neither names a buyer. Neither revises 0003, 0014 or 0015. Neither says anything about carve sizes other than 4096, about searched recipes, about more than seven families, or about content outside the corpus builder's families.

invocation: export OMP_NUM_THREADS=3 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=3 MKL_NUM_THREADS=3; nice -n 10 python3 tools/pivot/run_fdc.py --stage run --prereg-file prereg/0016-fdc-4096.json --cache data/pivot/full_c4096.npz --workdir artifacts/pivot/fdc_4096_ckpt --out artifacts/pivot/fdc_4096.json --scores-out artifacts/pivot/fdc_4096_scores.json; then python3 tools/readers/fdc4096_verdict.py. Relaunching the identical command after a container restart is the whole recovery procedure; checkpoints are committed and pushed as they land.

smoke.invocation: The invocation above with --smoke added and --workdir, --out and --scores-out pointed under the session scratchpad; the runner refuses --smoke with any output path under artifacts/ and a real run with any output path outside it. The smoke block replaces budget_chunks, repro_rows, null_rows and launch and keeps the full 800000-row pool at 840 chunks (a smoke at 1120 chunks with three roles completed before the fourth role was added; the fourth role's smoke is at 840 chunks) (a smaller pool holds only a row or two of each chunk, so chunk-budget folds would be too small to carry all 26 classes in their fit and validation rows, which the runner checks before any fit: two smoke attempts at 140 and 280 chunks were refused for that reason); everything else is the sealed protocol. The smoke's reproduction fits 0003's 10000-row rung rows exactly (0.1415 banked) and is compared with it informally in the engineering log; the reader voids every smoke run.
